notes: Fixes the root cause cleanly: new unexported `Token.isOpenCurlyBrace` and `Token.isCloseCurlyBrace` helpers ignore quoted braces, and every brace check in the dispenser and parser now uses them, including snippet and import detection, `blockTokens`, `addresses` and `directive`. It removes the now-redundant `wasQuoted` hack, adds solid dispenser and parser tests covering double quotes, backticks, nested blocks and error cases, and leaves only minor unexamined edge cases such as brace comparisons in other packages or env-expanded braces.

Adds `isOpenCurlyBrace`/`isCloseCurlyBrace` token helpers that ignore quoted braces and applies them consistently across the dispenser and parser (addresses, directives, import, blockTokens, `NextBlock`, `NextArg`, `ArgErr`), which removes the old ad-hoc `wasQuoted` check; it adds focused dispenser and parser tests covering quoted braces as args, nested blocks, backtick quoting and error cases.

The `--once` transform runs after config consolidation, which covers run, cloud and archive since they share the option flag set. It keeps exec, env, tags and browser options, clears the shortcut options, rejects multiple scenarios and errors on conflicting shortcut flags with the InvalidConfig exit code; unit and end-to-end tests are thorough, and only the env-var form of the shortcuts (e.g. K6_VUS) is left unchecked, which the issue does not require.

Adds `--once` to the shared option flag set, so it covers run, cloud run and archive, and applies the transform after consolidation as the issue asks; it keeps exec, env, tags and browser options, rejects multiple scenarios and shortcut flags with InvalidConfig, and is backed by unit, integration and archive tests, though shortcut values from env vars (e.g. K6_VUS) are silently discarded rather than rejected.

Applies the slugs of a section and all its ancestor sections to the directory of the section and every descendant page, including leaf-bundle resources and taxonomy/term pages. A new TargetPathDescriptor.Dir field carries this cleanly through CreateTargetPaths. A thorough integration test covers nested sections, non-section subdirectories and taxonomies; it does not cover interplay with permalinks config or DisablePathToLower.

Adds an optional `Dir` override to the target path descriptor, computed by walking ancestor sections and applying their slugs, so slugs on sections, taxonomies and terms flow down to descendant pages and resources. It falls back to the old behavior when no slug is set and is well tested, though calling `Parent()`/`CurrentSection()` during path creation adds some coupling and the `*pageState` type assertion fails silently if it doesn't match.

Fixes the round-trip by wrapping a parenthesised NumberLiteral in a Wrapped unary-ADD DurationExpr, aligns Pretty so it omits the no-op '+', and adds durationLiteralValue so the zero/negative and division/modulo-by-zero checks still fire on wrapped literals. The synthetic ADD node is a bit of a representation hack, and it moves `offset (5)` from the static offset path to the expression path; tests are thorough across printer, prettier, AST and error cases.

Wraps a parenthesised NumberLiteral in a synthetic unary-ADD DurationExpr with Wrapped=true, so all five issue cases round-trip. It also updates the >0, division-by-zero and modulo-by-zero checks (via durationLiteralValue) and the prettier, so wrapped literals don't bypass validation or print as '(+5m)'. The synthetic unary-plus node is a slight hack compared with a dedicated Wrapped flag, but it is contained, gated on the experimental flag in the unary path, and backed by thorough parse, error, printer and prettier tests.

Correctly finds the root cause: the dedup on ConfigResource made the first block win, and returning every block per module fixes the reported for_each and count case. It also changes FindImportStatements' public return type to a slice. Parent override is still decided per ConfigResource, so one parent import silently drops the child's imports for other instances, which may be why it passes only 1 of 3 hidden PR tests. The added unit and context tests are well constructed but assert that debatable override behavior.

Fixes the reported bug: FindImportStatements now returns every import block declared in the same module instead of keeping one per ConfigResource. It still overrides at the ConfigResource level across modules, so a parent block importing one instance (b[0]) silently drops a child's import of a different instance (b[1]), the same silent-discard pattern the issue complains about. The return-type change plus failing 2/3 hidden tests suggest it diverges on module-override semantics or the expected API. The tests are good: a plan-level for_each/count test and a refactoring fixture test.

The sentinel ReturnError design is sound: it is raised as a panic from evalCall, trapped at walkTemplate and executeWithState, passed through try, and turned into a value in the template store, which removes the old contextWrapper rewrite. However, it changes behaviour for an existing piped-return case, and the candidate weakened that test's expected error to 'error calling delimit' rather than preserving behaviour, which is likely why the package suite fails.

The design follows the issue: a ReturnError sentinel is raised from evalCall, recovered in walkTemplate and executeWithState, and turned into a value in the template store, with try and template/block handled. However, `{{ return }}` without a value in a partial now returns the rendered output instead of an empty string, and an existing test's error assertion was weakened to 'error calling delimit' to hide a changed error message; the suite still fails and one hidden test fails.
